81226.subject: Pump.fun Bets on Dubious Celebrity Trader to Reach the Mainstream
81226.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* [**Pump.fun**](https://thedefiant.io/news/tokens/kimchi-coin-minted-before-pump-fun-ad-fee-routing)[ ran a Kimchi coin ad 78 seconds after mint](https://thedefiant.io/news/tokens/kimchi-coin-minted-before-pump-fun-ad-fee-routing)

* [**NSA**](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/nsa-urges-php-users-to-patch-or-take-systems-offline)[ urges PHP patching or offline systems](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/nsa-urges-php-users-to-patch-or-take-systems-offline)

* [**Ledger**](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/ledger-adds-morpho-loans-against-wrapped-bitcoin)[ adds Morpho loans against wrapped bitcoin](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/ledger-adds-morpho-loans-against-wrapped-bitcoin)

* [**PancakeSwap**](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pancakeswap-opens-the-flip-vote-with-cake-supply-condition)[ votes on an 88% LP fee share](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pancakeswap-opens-the-flip-vote-with-cake-supply-condition)

* [**OCC**](https://thedefiant.io/converge/regulation/occ-finalizes-genius-act-rule-drops-third-party-yield-presumption)[ finalizes GENIUS rule, drops yield presumption](https://thedefiant.io/converge/regulation/occ-finalizes-genius-act-rule-drops-third-party-yield-presumption)

Pump.fun wants customers who have never heard of a bonding curve. On Tuesday it signed Kimchi, a pseudonymous trader who claims about $40 million of profit on the TRUMP token, as a creative partner, and posted an ad for a Kimchi coin 78 seconds after the coin was minted. Co-founder Alon Cohen said the platform's next wave of users "does not come from CT."

The push makes sense, because the memecoin market no longer hands Pump.fun its users by default. Launchpads on Robinhood Chain [cut its share of launchpad fees](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pump-fun-launchpad-fee-share-falls-robinhood-chain-pons-noxa) from 79% to 27% in two weeks this summer, and it climbed back above half by mid-August. Flap, a BNB Chain launchpad, [passed it in daily revenue](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/flap-overtakes-pump-fun-in-daily-revenue-with-1-18-million) on Aug. 1. Fomo, a trading app with copy trading and Apple Pay signup, [competes for the trade rather than the mint](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/fomo-s-record-revenue-week-still-trails-axiom-hyperliquid-and-pump-fun), and earned $19 million over the last 30 days against Pump.fun's $45.4 million. Pump.fun has answered by widening its app: [callout rewards tied to followers' profits](https://thedefiant.io/news/tokens/pump-fun-to-tie-callout-rewards-to-followers-profits), coins priced in tokenized stocks, and this week [pre-IPO tokens](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pump-fun-adds-pre-ipo-tokens-to-its-launch-pairings). A famous face is the next move.

The ads got a lot of backlash, but I think the message was right. People come to a memecoin launchpad for a shot at getting rich quickly, and an ad that says so is honest about what the product sells. The cars-a

81225.subject: Urgent: Railway Security Disclosure - Rotate Credentials
81225.body:
Railway Logo

Earlier this morning, Railway detected anomalous activity involving systems that store customer environment variables. After further investigation, our investigation to date indicates that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted environment variables and, for some of them, obtained the decrypted contents. Environment variables may contain secrets such as API keys or database and registry credentials.

We believe this is part of a series of attacks recently targeting platform companies with the aim of compromising AI inference providers. We have notified these upstream providers to revoke all keys proactively, as we take these kinds of events extremely seriously.

What you should do

* Immediately revoke and reissue all environment variables, including any API keys, stored in Railway.
* If you have any credentials on an external registry, .
* Review logs for those services for unusual activity.

Until builds are restored, you will not be able to roll out new versions. We apologize for this inconvenience. Follow this incident ( https://status.railway.com/incident/QH8L8B3E?utm_campaign=Security+Disclosure%3A+Wednesday+October+21st&utm_content=Security+Disclosure%3A+Wednesday+October+21st&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ) to be notified when builds resume and for further updates.

We will provide new updates on this announcement, and on status.railway.com ( https://status.railway.com?utm_campaign=Security+Disclosure%3A+Wednesday+October+21st&utm_content=Security+Disclosure%3A+Wednesday+October+21st&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ) as we gather all facts about the scope of impact.

Manage email preferences ( https://railway.com/account/notifications?utm_campaign=Security+Disclosure%3A+Wednesday+October+21st&utm_content=Security+Disclosure%3A+Wednesday+October+21st&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io )

81070.subject: 💰 The Funding: What happens if MSCI drops crypto treasuries like Strategy?
81070.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c1c9af72-58d8-47c5-88eb-8e5007f7e3dc/unnamed__17_.png?t=1789144554)
Caption: 

Written by Yogita Khatri  | Edited by Zack Abrams

———————————————————————————

Presented By:

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0f002faa-88b1-4362-8467-fbc25a6c61ee/Screenshot_2026-10-16_at_4.02.56_PM__3___1___1___1_.png?t=1792184177)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

----------
Happy Sunday, and welcome to the 62nd edition of [The Funding](https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding)!

MSCI [finalized rules](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-15-msci-rules-could-exclude-strategy-mstr-from-indexes-418729) on Oct. 15 that could push Strategy and other crypto treasury companies out of its main global indexes as soon as Nov. 30. What would that mean for how these companies raise money, and is anyone still willing to fund them? I caught up with investors and analysts to find out.

Let's get into it.


----------———————————————————————————

----------
# THE INSIDE VIEW

## What if MSCI drops crypto treasuries?


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2012e140-bc90-4ae9-b029-9f403353161b/Dat-Image-1200x675.jpg?t=1792371900)
Caption: 

----------
Index provider MSCI recently [approved new rules](https://app2.msci.com/webapp/index_ann/DocGet?pub_key=aq0wbkjxPgo%3D&lang=en&format=html) that target "non-operating" companies, which mainly hold assets instead of running a business, such as digital asset treasury firms, or DATs.

Under the new rules, MSCI will first check whether a company has substantial operating assets, such as equipment or inventory. In the [proposal MSCI published in August](https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/indexes/consultations/equity/Consultation%20on%20Eligibility%20of%20Non-Operating%20Companies%20for%20the%20%20MSCI%20Global%20Investable%20Market%20Indexes.pdf), that meant operating assets making up more than half of total assets. Companies that fail this check face five financial tests, which in the proposal included whether a company generates operating cash flow and how much it relies on raising capital to buy assets. Those flagged on four or more will be excluded.

Current index members get some leeway: they will be removed only if they fail in both of their two most recent annual filing periods. If they fail in only one, they stay in the index unless they fail the following year. Companies not yet in the index are blocked if they fail in either of the last two years.

In a simulation published in August using May data, MSCI flagged two bitcoin treasury companies, Michael Saylor's Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet, for potential exclusion. Ethereum treasury firm SharpLink

80931.subject: Team1 Japan: Institutions Chose Avalanche. Now It’s the Builders’ Turn.
80931.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/team1-japan-institutions-chose-avalanche

Team1 Japan is officially here.
Our mission is to build a Japanese builder community that matches the scale of Japan’s institutional adoption.
Here is what that means, and why Japan’s builder scene is unique.
The sequence is backwards, and that’s the opportunity
Japan’s institutions have already made their choice.
Progmat, the platform behind the majority of the country’s security token issuance, moved billions in tokenized real estate and corporate bonds onto a dedicated Avalanche L1. TIS, which processes more than half of Japan’s credit card volume, also launched its own L1. Some of the largest names in Japanese finance are now exploring tokenized government bonds using Avalanche infrastructure.
In most countries, this runs the other way. A community forms, developers experiment, projects ship, and eventually, sometimes years later, institutions notice and follow. Japan skipped the first half.
The chains themselves stay controlled, as Japanese financial regulation requires, but they no longer sit behind a wall. Gateways outward to wallets, to stablecoin settlement, and to applications written by people who were never invited into a private consortium are now being built. Japan’s financial system is no longer a closed circuit. It is growing an edge you can build against.
The demand is real, and the gateways to these platforms are underway.
That’s the gap Team1 Japan is here to close.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
What is Team1?
Team1 is a network of builders, developers, creators, event organizers, and community leaders working to grow the Avalanche ecosystem from the ground up. Since launching in 2024, it has grown to hundreds of members across more than 40 countries, with official chapters now live in the USA, Vietnam, India, Türkiye, Brasil, and across LatAm.
Team1 Japan is the newest of those chapters.
Our mandate is focused: connect Japan’s builders to Avalanche, and connect them to each other.
This is a formalization, not a beginning
Japan’s Avalanche community has been meeting for years.
Since April 2023, over 30 events have been held across Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, and Fukuoka with more than 1200 attendees between them. The anchor is Avalanche Gourmet Night, a series running for over two years that marks the beginning of the Avalanche community’s in-person presence
The programming has widened past meetups. Avalanche Academy study sessions have run four times since March, giving developers a recurring technical space rather than a social one. There have been collaborations with Uniswap Labs, zeroone, and Pudgy Penguins, and a workshop for teams who entered the JPYC stablecoin innovation challenge.

80805.subject: More Trading, Different Activity: Avalanche’s Latest 30 Days
80805.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/more-trading-different-activity-avalanches

Nansen recorded 48.4 million transactions, down 33% from the previous 30 days. At the same time, DEX volume climbed to $2.7 billion, up 145%, while active users increased 8.1% to 1.6 million.
So Avalanche was not simply quieter. There were fewer transactions in Nansen’s dataset, but much more trading volume. Users still grew, capital continued moving through the ecosystem, and activity across individual Avalanche L1s adds another part of the picture.
Trading picked up fast
The biggest change is DEX volume. WAVAX alone accounted for around $2.5 billion, with roughly $1.3 billion in buys and $1.3 billion in sells.
Active users also moved higher, reaching around 1.6 million, up 8.1% from the previous period. If that user growth continues while transactions stabilize, this month may end up looking more like a change in how Avalanche is being used than a simple drop in activity.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
AVAX and WAVAX are moving differently
Around $4.6 million of native AVAX left exchange wallets over the latest seven days. WAVAX went the other way. Around $12.3 million moved into exchanges, while Top PnL wallets reduced their WAVAX positions by roughly $2.2 million.
Native AVAX is moving away from exchanges while WAVAX is moving toward them. At the same time, WAVAX remains extremely active on DEXs. For now, it looks more like capital moving around the ecosystem than everyone taking the same position.
Fresh wallets are still bringing money in
Fresh wallets added approximately $20.8 million in AVAX over seven days. Another $16.3 million went into WAVAX. Those are meaningful inflows, but both were below their normal levels. AVAX was running at around 0.6x its average flow, while WAVAX was around 0.4x.
New wallets are participating, just not at an unusually high rate. There is fresh capital coming in, but this does not look like another sudden wave of adoption.
BTC.b is still doing real volume
BTC.b continues to be one of the more active parts of Avalanche DeFi. It recorded around $238.8 million in DEX volume over 30 days, with approximately $1.3 million in net flow.
Over the latest seven days, BTC.b generated another $60.9 million in volume, with $31.5 million in buys and $29.4 million in sells.
There is no major imbalance between buyers and sellers. It is simply an active market.
Bitcoin liquidity gives Avalanche another source of capital beyond AVAX and stablecoins, and BTC.b is still moving through the ecosystem rather than simply sitting in wallets.
sAVAX looks steady
sAVAX has around 16,609 holders, approximately $169.8 million in market cap, and roughly $2.2 million in liquidity. Seven-day volume was around $743,000, with approximately $424,000 in buys compared with $319,000 in sells.
There is no obvious new staking surge here.
